title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The student (EE1) shares their personal identity information (student id) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) during the login and submission process. This act of sharing causes a threat because the portal can identify the student uniquely.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure
description: The student (EE1) shares sensitive personal data (work file, course, submission timestamp) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1). This act of sharing causes a threat because the portal can access and potentially misuse this sensitive information.

title: Data Processing for Identification
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the student's data and processes it to identify the student. This action at the destination causes a threat because the portal can link the submitted data to the student's identity.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The portal element (P1) shares the student's unique identifier (student id) with the assignment & grading service (P2) without any authentication or authorization check. This allows P2 to potentially identify the specific student associated with the request.
assumptions: The portal assumes the student id is a unique identifier and that the service will process it as a valid student reference.

title: Course and File Reference Disclosure
description: The portal element (P1) shares the course identifier and file reference with the assignment & grading service (P2). This allows P2 to link the request to a specific course and potentially access or modify files associated with that course.
assumptions: The portal assumes the course and file reference are valid and that the service will process them as valid course and file identifiers.

title: Requesting Role Disclosure
description: The portal element (P1) shares the requesting role with the assignment & grading service (P2). This allows P2 to determine the specific role of the requester (e.g., student, instructor, administrator) and potentially apply role-based access controls or privileges.
assumptions: The portal assumes the requesting role is a valid role and that the service will process it as a valid role identifier.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The assignment & grading service (P2) receives the student id, course, and file reference and processes them in a way that allows unauthorized access or modification of the student's data or files.
assumptions: The service assumes the received data is sufficient to perform its intended grading and assignment functions without additional validation.

title: Data Linking for Identification
description: The assignment & grading service (P2) receives the student id and course identifier and uses them to link the request to a specific student, potentially enabling identification of the requester beyond the role.
assumptions: The service assumes the combination of student id and course identifier uniquely identifies the requester.

title: Assignment File Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares the assignment file with the Assignment Store (DS1) without verifying the recipient's identity or authorization. This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to an entity that may not be intended to receive it.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The destination element (DataStore DS1) receives the assignment file and stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat. The store may process or store the data without proper access controls, potentially exposing student information to unauthorized parties.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The teacher (EE3) shares their identity information with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) during the login process. This allows the portal to potentially identify the teacher and associate their data with their specific courses.
assumptions: The login process requires the teacher to authenticate and provide their credentials.

title: Data Processing for Identification
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the teacher's identity information and uses it to identify the teacher and associate their data with their specific courses for processing.
assumptions: The portal has the capability to link the teacher's identity to their course data.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The portal shares student names and work content with the teacher, which may allow the teacher to identify specific students and access their private work.
assumptions: The teacher has access to the portal and the data is not encrypted or pseudonymized.

title: Student Work Content Exposure
description: The portal shares student work content with the teacher, which may allow the teacher to access private or sensitive information.
assumptions: The teacher has access to the portal and the data is not encrypted or pseudonymized.

title: Teacher Identity Disclosure
description: The teacher (EE3) shares their identity information (teacher id) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) to facilitate the recording of the grade and feedback. This act of sharing causes the threat because the recipient (P1) can now identify the teacher, potentially linking them to other data or compromising their privacy.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The teacher (EE3) shares their student id with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) to record the grade and feedback. This act of sharing causes the threat because the recipient (P1) can now identify the student, potentially linking them to other data or compromising their privacy.

title: Grader Identity Disclosure
description: The teacher (EE3) shares their grader id with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) to record the grade and feedback. This act of sharing causes the threat because the recipient (P1) can now identify the grader, potentially linking them to other data or compromising their privacy.

title: Data Processing for Identity Linking
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the teacher's identity (EE3) and student id (EE3) and processes them to link the teacher to the student. This action causes the threat because the data is stored in a way that allows the teacher to be identified by the student, potentially violating the principle of anonymity.

title: Data Processing for Grader Linking
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the teacher's grader id (EE3) and processes it to link the teacher to the grader. This action causes the threat because the data is stored in a way that allows the teacher to be identified by the grader, potentially violating the principle of anonymity.

title: Student ID Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares the student ID with the destination element (DataStore DS2) without any authentication or encryption. This allows the destination to potentially identify the student.
assumptions: The process does not validate the student ID before sharing.

title: Course and Grade Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares the course and grade information with the destination element (DataStore DS2) without any authentication or encryption. This allows the destination to potentially identify the student and the specific course/grade.
assumptions: The process does not validate the course or grade before sharing.

title: Feedback and Grader ID Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares the feedback and grader ID information with the destination element (DataStore DS2) without any authentication or encryption. This allows the destination to potentially identify the student and the specific grader.
assumptions: The process does not validate the feedback or grader ID before sharing.

title: Timestamp Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares the timestamp information with the destination element (DataStore DS2) without any authentication or encryption. This allows the destination to potentially identify the student and the specific time the grade was recorded.
assumptions: The process does not validate the timestamp before sharing.

title: Data Storage and Processing
description: The destination element (DataStore DS2) receives the grade record and stores it in a way that allows for potential identification of the student. For example, if the database is indexed by student ID, the data can be used to link or identify the student.
assumptions: The database does not use additional metadata to identify the student.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The student (EE1) shares their personal identity information with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) to request grades and feedback.

title: Data Processing for Personal Information
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the student's identity information and processes it to generate grades and feedback, which may reveal sensitive personal data.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The portal shares the student's unique identifier (e.g., student ID or email) with the external entity (Student) without explicit consent or a clear, opt-in mechanism for the student to control this sharing.

title: Teacher Feedback Data Leakage
description: The portal shares teacher feedback data (which may contain sensitive information about the student's academic performance or behavior) with the external entity (Student) without proper authorization or privacy safeguards.

title: Data Processing and Storage Risk
description: Upon receipt, the Student entity may process or store the shared data in a way that creates new privacy risks, such as aggregating multiple students' grades or storing sensitive feedback in a centralized database that could be accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Identity Confusion
description: The parent entity (EE2) shares its identity with the child entity (EE1) without explicit authentication or authorization. This allows the child to potentially impersonate the parent or access data associated with the parent's identity.
assumptions: The parent account is linked to the child account, and the system does not enforce strict identity separation between them.

title: Data Processing Disclosure
description: The process (P1) processes the parent's identity information (EE2) and the child's identity information (EE1) to generate grades. This processing step may reveal sensitive identity data to unauthorized parties or for unintended purposes.
assumptions: The process does not have sufficient controls to mask or anonymize the identity data before processing.

title: Grade Data Exposure
description: The portal element (P1) shares the child's grade data with the parent (EE2) without any authentication or authorization checks. This allows the parent to access sensitive personal information.
assumptions: The portal is configured to display grades to any external entity.

title: Feedback Data Exposure
description: The portal element (P1) shares feedback data with the parent (EE2) without any authentication or authorization checks. This allows the parent to access sensitive personal information.
assumptions: The portal is configured to display feedback to any external entity.

title: Submission History Exposure
description: The portal element (P1) shares the child's submission history with the parent (EE2) without any authentication or authorization checks. This allows the parent to access sensitive personal information.
assumptions: The portal is configured to display submission history to any external entity.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The parent (EE2) receives the grades, feedback, and submission history and stores/processes them in a way that causes a privacy threat. The parent may use this data for its own purposes without the child's consent.
assumptions: The parent has no explicit consent to receive and process this specific data.

title: Account Creation Unauthorized
description: ExternalEntity EE4 (School Administrator) creates an account without proper authorization or verification, leading to potential unauthorized access to the system.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure
description: EE4 shares sensitive personal information (names, emails, roles) with the Grades Portal Web App without adequate data masking or encryption.

title: Data Processing Disclosure
description: Process P1 (Grades Portal Web App) processes and stores account and relationship data in a way that could be used to identify users or infer sensitive attributes.

title: Data Linking and Re-identification
description: P1 may link or re-identify users across different data flows or systems by correlating email addresses, names, and roles, creating a comprehensive profile.

title: Data Leakage
description: The source element (Process P2) shares account records and parent-child relationship links with the Account Directory (DataStore DS3). This act of sharing causes the threat because the destination element (DS3) may store, process, or disseminate this data in ways that compromise privacy, such as by making the data available to unauthorized users or entities.
assumptions: The process P2 is configured to write data to DS3 without additional access controls or encryption.

title: Data Misuse
description: The destination element (DataStore DS3) receives the account records and parent-child relationship links. The threat arises because the destination may store, process, or disseminate this data in ways that compromise privacy, such as by making the data available to unauthorized users or entities.
assumptions: The data store DS3 is configured to store data without additional access controls or encryption.

title: Data Leakage
description: The source element (Process P2) shares full grade records, assignments, and account directory with the external cloud hosting provider (EE5) without any encryption or access controls. This act of sharing causes the threat of unauthorized data access.

title: Data in Transit
description: The data flow (DF14) transmits sensitive grade records, assignments, and account directory information over the network. This data-centric threat arises from the transmission of unencrypted data, potentially allowing interception or metadata-based identification.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The destination element (Cloud Hosting Provider EE5) receives and processes the data without proper authorization or safeguards. This action causes the threat of data misuse or storage in a way that compromises privacy.

title: Grade Records Access
description: The source element (DataStore DS2) shares grade records with the Assignment & Grading Service (Process P2). This act of sharing causes the threat because the destination element (P2) may process or store the data in a way that causes the threat.

title: Data Processing at Destination
description: The destination element (Process P2) receives the grade records and processes them to build student, parent, and teacher views. This processing may cause the threat if the views are used to identify or link individuals inappropriately.
